components.note: Online before each lecture; three submissions allowed until the 8 PM deadline the day before.
Two required in-class exams plus one optional cumulative exam that can replace a lower exam grade.
About six assignments; one free extension of up to two days.
About three class days of exercises turned in for credit.
Groups of two present a journal paper, 12-15 minutes.

grading.scale: A+ 95-100; A 90-94.99; A- 85-89.99; middle bands cut from excerpt; F below 50.
grading.drop: The optional December 9 cumulative exam can replace a lower exam grade.

exams.name: Optional cumulative exam
exams.note: can replace a lower exam grade

ATMS 420.finalExam: No separate final; the optional cumulative exam is on December 9, the last day of class.

materials.item: Introduction to Atmospheric Chemistry, Daniel J. Jacob, 2nd ed. (main text, online)
Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, Seinfeld and Pandis (2016)
Chemistry of the Upper and Lower Atmosphere, Finlayson-Pitts
Modeling of Atmospheric Chemistry, Brasseur and Jacob (2017)

ATMS 420.attendance: Designed for in-person, synchronous attendance; in-class exercise days are turned in for credit. If ill, contact the instructor right away.
ATMS 420.lateWork: One free homework extension of up to two days; other late rules not given in excerpt.
other: AI tools are allowed only in the 2 in-class coding activities; any other use is academic dishonesty.
During exams the instructor provides printed textbook copies; no other materials allowed.
Collaboration on homework must be acknowledged in writing; each student writes their own solutions.
Homework is handwritten or tablet, submitted by scan or PDF.
